primitives.note: Unshackled stacks up to 3 (4s duration each, refreshing on cast) granting 125% bonus attack speed while stacked; casting any ability generates a stack
Next basic attack consumes a stack to become an uncancellable, empowered whirl dealing magic damage to the primary target and reduced magic damage to nearby enemies
Petricite Burst's primary-target damage can critically strike (wiki-noted bug: 175% instead of intended 200%); no crit on secondary targets
Q's initial converging-chain hit and W's dash-strike each deal magic damage on cast/short delay, on cooldown, for mana
Chain Lash has two separately timed damage instances: the initial chain hit, then a 0.6s-delayed explosion at the intersection point
Abscond (no damage, sets up) followed within a 3.5s window by Abduct (the actual chain-hit damage + dash), functioning as a two-part ability
Kingslayer's self-heal scales with Sylas's own missing health, from a minimum to a doubled maximum heal; relevant to the survival fight's damage-taken accounting
Mana costs on all four active abilities can meaningfully cap the number of casts achievable within the 15s window
Hijack's per-target cooldown (200% of the target's base ultimate cooldown, minimum 40s, starting on steal) effectively prevents casting R twice on the same dummy within a 15s fight
Hijacked abilities that lack an AP ratio have their AD ratios converted into AP ratios scaling off Sylas's own total/bonus AD

needsBespoke.why: R (Hijack) steals a copy of the targeted enemy champion's ultimate ability, and its damage/behavior entirely depends on which champion's kit is copied. The primitive list cannot express an arbitrary borrowed ability's mechanics; simulating R's offensive contribution against a stationary dummy (which likely has no ultimate to steal) requires a bespoke assumption about what, if anything, R contributes to the damage fight.

unsettled.question: Does Hijack contribute any direct damage in the dummy fight, given the target is a stationary dummy rather than a champion with a stealable, damage-dealing ultimate?
options: Exclude R from the damage fight entirely (only its own cast contributes an Unshackled stack; no stolen-ultimate damage is modeled)
Assume some generic/average stolen ultimate and model its damage using the AD-to-AP conversion rules
Assume R is never cast in the damage fight since no valid steal target/ability exists

unsettled.question: What is the correct missing-health breakpoint for Kingslayer's heal to reach its maximum (2x) value: the bin's SylasW.MaxExecuteThreshold=0.4 (40% missing health) or the wiki's stated 0 to 60% missing health scaling?
options: Use bin value: heal reaches max at 40% missing health
Use wiki value: heal reaches max at 60% missing health

unsettled.question: Does casting E (Abscond then Abduct) generate one Unshackled stack for the whole combo, or two separate stack-generating events (one per ability activation, since the bin lists SylasE and SylasE2 as distinct spells)?
options: Abscond and Abduct each independently generate/refresh a stack (two events from one E use)
The Abscond→Abduct sequence is treated as a single ability activation granting one stack

unsettled.question: Does Kingslayer's 0.5s 'queue time' function like a cast time that delays the dash/strike and locks Sylas out of other actions, or is it a targeting-only queue with the ability otherwise resolving near-instantly (consistent with its stated 'cast time = none')?
options: Treat the 0.5s as an effective cast/action-lock delaying the damage instance
Treat 'cast time = none' as authoritative and ignore the queue time for pacing purposes

proposal: Enter the fight at max ranks with an Unshackled stack window already primed (auto-attack once beforehand if allowed, to have the empowered Petricite Burst attack ready).
Open with Abscond into Abduct (E) to close distance, generate/refresh an Unshackled stack, and land its magic-damage hit.
Immediately follow with Kingslayer (W) to dash-strike the dummy for magic damage and refresh the Unshackled stack window.
Weave in the empowered basic attack (consumes a stack for bonus magic damage via Petricite Burst) whenever a stack is available.
Cast Chain Lash (Q) at the dummy for its initial magic damage, then let the 0.6s-delayed explosion land as a separate damage instance while continuing basic attacks.
Cast Hijack (R) once, primarily to bank an extra Unshackled stack from the cast; recast its stolen ability only if the dossier's ruling on R's damage contribution allows it.
Repeat E → W → Q on cooldown for the remainder of the 15s window, filling every gap with empowered/basic attacks, respecting each ability's mana cost against Sylas's mana pool.
questions: Should R be included in the optimal rotation at all, or omitted given the dummy fight offers no meaningful stealable ultimate?
Does the simulator assume abilities are already at max rank for the whole 15s fight, or does leveling occur during it (affecting Q/W/E/R damage values used in the rotation)?
Is Sylas assumed to open already in range of the dummy, or does he need to spend part of the 15s closing distance with E before any damage lands?

Should the rotation prioritize maximizing raw damage output (favoring Q/W/E on cooldown) or maximizing empowered-attack uptime (favoring auto-attack weaving), if the two conflict under mana constraints?
